title: 22nd ICE Custody Death of 2026: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo Dies at Delaney Hall, NJ
excerpt: Edwin Jovanny Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old Salvadoran immigrant, died at University Hospital in Newark after collapsing at the Delaney Hall ICE detention facility—marking the 22nd ICE custody death of 2026 and the second fatality at that facility. His family alleged he had been denied medication for epilepsy, diabetes, and high blood pressure.
content:
On August 1, 2026, Edwin Jovanny Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old citizen of El Salvador who had lived in New Jersey for over 20 years, died at University Hospital in Newark after collapsing in Delaney Hall's cafeteria complaining of dizziness and fatigue.

Lopez-Cornejo's family alleged he had been denied medication for epilepsy, diabetes, and high blood pressure while a federal habeas corpus petition was active before a judge. ICE stated he received proper medical care and that emergency services were called, but that responders arrived roughly 37 minutes after the 911 call. His death marked the 22nd ICE custody death in 2026—with four months remaining in the year—and the second at the Delaney Hall facility alone.

  • A prior Gothamist investigation in June 2026 had found that more than 70 detainees at Delaney Hall had filed federal lawsuits alleging medical neglect, with more than 30 claiming they were denied prescribed medication for chronic conditions including asthma, epilepsy, diabetes, and cancer.
  • In 2025, 33 people died in ICE custody—the highest annual total in more than two decades, according to the National Immigration Project. The 2026 pace was tracking to surpass that record.
  • Newark Mayor Ras Baraka condemned the death and renewed calls for the facility's closure.
  • ACLU-NJ Executive Director Amol Sinha called the death "another devastating result of the rampant inhumane conditions at Delaney Hall."
